title: ASTU 3rd Round Model Exit Exam 2026
source: ASTU Software Engineering — 3rd Round Model Exit Examination 2026 (2hr, 100 MCQs)

focusGuide.Fundamentals of Programming: C++ arrays, pointers, references, I/O, memory (stack/heap), file modes.
focusGuide.Data Structures: Stacks, queues, deques, arrays, circular queues, tree traversals.
focusGuide.Java / OOP: Abstract classes, interfaces, inheritance, constructors, event-driven programming.
focusGuide.Web Development: HTML/CSS/JS stack, HTTP, Django, SOA, microservices, session management.
focusGuide.Android: Fragments, Room, RecyclerView, mobile security, ethical framework choice.
focusGuide.Database: ACID, ER diagrams, DBMS, concurrency, weak entities, OODBMS.
focusGuide.Operating Systems: fork(), PCB, scheduling, Banker's algorithm, file allocation, synchronization.
focusGuide.Software Engineering: SDLC, modularity, requirements engineering, scope creep, black-box testing.
focusGuide.Software Architecture: Singleton, Mediator, cohesion/coupling, architecture documentation, NFRs.
focusGuide.Project Management: COCOMO, Scrum/SRS, risk, lag, regression vs corrective maintenance.
focusGuide.Software Testing: Functional testing, ISO 25010 usability, Law of Demeter, ACT, exit criteria.
focusGuide.Software Maintenance: Perfective maintenance, reverse engineering, CFG/call graphs.
focusGuide.Networking: Private IP, DHCP, OSI layers, subnet masks, TCP/IP, ACL, bus topology.
focusGuide.AI / ML: Bayesian inference, utility agents, BFS, A*, Turing Test, knowledge representation.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly declares an array of 10 integers in C++?
questions.concept: Key idea (Fundamentals of Programming): int arr[10];

questions.text: What does the expression *(ptr + i) represent in C++?

questions.concept: Key idea (Fundamentals of Programming): if

questions.concept: Key idea (Fundamentals of Programming): value_2

questions.concept: Key idea (Fundamentals of Programming): Garbage value

questions.text: Which of the following correctly dynamically allocates memory for an array of 10 integers in C++?
questions.concept: Key idea (Fundamentals of Programming): int *arr = new int[10];

options.text: The array is allocated on the stack and will be destroyed when the function returns
Arrays cannot be returned from functions in C++
The array size is not specified in the return type
Integer arrays require dynamic allocation to be returned

questions.concept: Key idea (Fundamentals of Programming): The array is allocated on the stack and will be destroyed when the function returns

questions.text: What is the fundamental difference between stack and heap memory allocation in C++?

options.text: Stack allocation is slower but more flexible; heap allocation is faster but limited in size
Stack allocation is automatic with fixed lifetime (scope-based); heap allocation is manual with dynamic lifetime
Stack is used for global variables; heap is used for local variables
Stack memory can only store primitive types; heap can store any data type

questions.concept: Key idea (Fundamentals of Programming): Stack allocation is automatic with fixed lifetime (scope-based); heap allocation is manual with dynamic lifetime

questions.text: Which of the following is true about a circular queue?

questions.text: What is the primary difference between an Abstract Class and an Interface?

options.text: Abstract classes can have constructors, while interfaces cannot.
Interfaces can have private methods, while abstract classes cannot.
A class can extend multiple abstract classes but only one interface.
Abstract classes only contain static variables.

questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): Abstract classes can have constructors, while interfaces cannot.

questions.text: If class `Manager` inherits from class `Employee`, and `Employee` inherits from `Person`, this is an example of:
questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): Multilevel Inheritance

questions.text: What is the result of attempting to instantiate an abstract class?

options.text: The program runs and creates an empty object.
The compiler throws an error because the class is incomplete.
The JVM creates a default implementation at runtime.
The object is created but all its methods are null.

questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): The compiler throws an error because the class is incomplete.

questions.text: When a subclass constructor does not explicitly call a superclass constructor, what does the Java compiler do?

options.text: It inserts an implicit call to `super()`.
It initializes only the static members of the superclass.

questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): It inserts an implicit call to `super()`.
